newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus shipping quality may help offshore status.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus shipping quality may help offshore status.

text.p: The quality of Cyprus' shipping register could help in preserving the island's status as a leading offshore centre when it becomes a member of the European Union, a Cypriot official said on Saturday.

"The existing system will not be altered before the accession of Cyprus to the European Union, but even then it will be sought that any inevitable amendments be made gradually, in the longest period possible," Cypriot Communications and Works Minister Adamos Adamides told the annual general meeting of the Cyprus Shipping Council (CSC).

Shipping companies constitute an integral part of Cyprus' offshore sector, which offers a lower rate of taxation compared with local companies -- an issue that may be considered discriminatory under EU competition regulations.
The island, which applied for EU membership in 1990, is due to start accession negotiations with the bloc next year.

"There are indications that if we succeed our targets which concern the improvement in quality of the Cyprus merchant fleet, our chances to obtain a more favourable stand by the EU on our taxation system on shipping will definitely be increased," Adamides said.
The eastern Mediterranean island boosts a shipping registry of 2,700 vessels with 27 million gross tonnes, making it the fourth largest in the world.
In recent years Cyprus has applied concerted efforts to shake off the image of being a "flag of convenience" with the adoption of international conventions setting minumum safety standards.
The island is currently expanding its network of surveyors in key maritime centres and boosting its merchant shipping department.
Recently the communications and works minister was empowered to strike vessels off the Cyprus registry if they did not meet safety standards. Three have been struck off the list this year.
Klaus Oldendorff, outgoing chairman of the CSC, told the conference the body was disappointed with the slow pace of boosting the shipping department.
Implementation of international conventions setting minimum safety and training standards would place additional burdens on the department, he said.
"The government... must take the necessary measures to ensure that the shipping department is able to comply with the additional loads it has to carry," he said.
The CSC has 117 member companies whose vessels fly the Cyprus flag.
